title: Constructor Invoking Virtual Method (Uninitialized Fields)
pattern: A base class constructor calls a virtual method on itself. A derived class overrides that virtual method and reads or mutates derived-class-specific member variables in its implementation.
why_bad: In object-oriented languages like C++, base class constructors execute *before* derived class constructors. When the base class constructor calls the virtual method, it resolves to the derived class's override, which attempts to access derived-class members (like pointer `c`) before the derived class constructor has run to initialize them. This results in undefined behavior or a null-pointer crash.
detection: Identify any invocation of a `virtual` method inside a class constructor. Ensure that any derived class overrides this virtual method and accesses subclass-specific members.
counterexample: A base class calling a non-virtual private method inside its constructor.
fix: Never call virtual methods within constructors. Instead, separate initialization from construction using a static creation factory or an explicit post-construction setup call.
source: Michael Feathers, *Working Effectively with Legacy Code*, page 294 / passage [294, 650].
